 Elasticsearch powers search, observability, and AI retrieval (RAG) for the world's largest organizations. We are seeking a Principal Software Engineer to join the Elasticsearch Performance team. In this role, you will lead architectural and code-level performance engineering initiatives. Your goal is to drive the continuous optimization and predictability of Elasticsearch performance, partnering with area-specific teams to unlock the full potential of our software.
 What You Will Be Doing 
 Owning core performance engineering initiatives from architecture to production, focusing on the delivery of high-impact optimizations. Leading the technical design, plan, and execution for major architectural and code-level performance improvements.
 Developing foundational performance models and methodologies for complex, distributed systems.
 Driving optimization strategies to ensure Elasticsearch remains performant, predictable, and scalable in diverse environments.
 Profiling and analyzing system behavior to identify bottlenecks in logging, metrics, vector search, and ES|QL.
 Ensuring robust performance benchmarks and regression detection for both stateful and stateless (Serverless) architectures.
 Collaborating across the company to embed performance-first thinking into new features from the outset.

 You have a solid comprehension of distributed systems architecture, including partition tolerance, cluster state propagation, and scaling challenges in large-scale data stores.
 You have a proven track record of using AI or advanced tooling to accelerate optimization, debug complex performance issues, and automate benchmarking workflows.
 You possess the ability to collaborate across functions and teams, acting as a force multiplier for performance engineering across the organization.
 You possess the ability to collaborate across functions and teams and seamlessly transition between different projects, codebases, or teams based on business priorities
 You can work autonomously, drive decisions and result in a distributed team by leveraging asynchronous, direct, and transparent communication.

 Experience integrating high-performance native libraries (e.g., C++, Rust, SIMD-accelerated code) into Java applications.
 Deep knowledge of modern storage engine performance, index modes, or vector search optimizations.
 Experience defining and managing Performance SLAs and success criteria for distributed systems.
 Experience working on the internals of a large-scale data store or search engine.
 Experience working on the internals of a data store or search engine.

About Vocantas 
 Vocantas provides workforce engagement and communication solutions for organizations where responsiveness and reliability are critical. Its platform helps customers improve staff communication, automate scheduling and outreach workflows, and increase operational efficiency. Vocantas supports organizations across North America in streamlining their processes and improving the experience for their staff and the people they serve. 
 Vocantas is part of Fluent Software Group (a Valsoft Corporation operating group), a global acquirer and operator of vertical market software businesses. We focus on specialized industries where expertise creates lasting advantages. 
 The Opportunity 
 Vocantas is looking for a Technical Account Manager to make sure our customers succeed after they buy, partnering with the Account Executive who owns each account. This role blends hands-on support, adoption strategy and product expertise. You’ll triage and resolve customer issues, work with internal teams to move them forward, present insights at QBRs, and identify opportunities to expand. 
 You’ll also have an opportunity to improve how the team operates by spotting gaps, suggesting practical solutions, and helping build stronger customer success processes as the organization evolves. 
 Location: Canada (remote) 
 While we aim to keep to regular business hours, this role requires the flexibility to support customers outside those hours, and across time zones, when urgent issues arise. 
 The salary for this role is $60,000–75,000 per year, plus an annual performance bonus and an uncapped expansion incentive. Final compensation will be determined based on experience, skills, and qualifications. 
 What You’ll Own 
 Customer Support  
 Act as the first point of contact when customers in your portfolio experience an issue or need assistance. 
 Troubleshoot and resolve support tickets, bringing in Support, Product or Engineering when an issue needs their expertise. 
 Manage customer escalations and sensitive situations with clear communication and consistent follow-through. 
 Triage, Prioritization & Internal Communication  
 Triage and prioritize customer issues and activities across your portfolio to meet service commitments. 
 Work with Support, Product and Engineering on complex issues, providing the context needed to move them toward resolution, and keep customers informed throughout. 
 Track customer commitments, open action items, and internal follow-ups through to completion. 
 Engagement & Adoption Strategy  
 Lead onboarding activities for Enterprise customers, including milestone planning, progress tracking, and adoption support. 
 Build strong customer relationships through proactive communication, regular engagement, and a clear understanding of each customer’s needs. 
 Identify at-risk accounts early through customer feedback, usage trends, and engagement patterns, and proactively drive recovery plans. 
 QBRs & Account Strategy  
 Partner with the Account Executive on structured Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) focused on customer outcomes, adoption, and future priorities. 
 Present usage and value insights, and follow through on the action items that come out of each review. 
 Expansion & Renewals  
 Identify expansion opportunities across your accounts and support the Account Executive through to close. 
 Support renewal conversations with insight into account health, risks and value delivered. 
 Product Expertise & Continuous Improvement  
 Develop deep expertise in the Vocantas platform and serve as a trusted advisor, guiding customers on best practices and training them to get the most out of the product. 
 Look for gaps, inefficient processes, or recurring customer issues and bring forward practical solutions to improve how the team works. 
 Collaborate closely with Product, Engineering, Support, and Sales to address customer needs and improve the overall customer experience. 
 Contribute to the development of customer success processes, playbooks, and AI-supported workflows. 
 What We’re Looking For 
 3–5 years of experience in Technical Account Management, Customer Success, or a similar customer-facing role within a B2B SaaS environment. 
 Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to work with customers by email and phone, lead meetings, and deliver training. 
 Comfortable troubleshooting and resolving a range of technical issues, and knowing when to bring in other teams. 
 Ability to triage and prioritize competing customer issues and activities. 
 Experience managing customer relationships, escalations, and onboarding and adoption initiatives. 
 Comfortable presenting data and insights to customer stakeholders. 
 Experience identifying expansion opportunities and supporting a sales partner through to close.

 Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities at once. 
 Experience working cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Support, and Sales teams. 
 A proactive, solution-oriented mindset: you notice what is not working, bring forward ideas, and follow through on improvements. 
 Strongly Preferred  
 Experience serving customers in healthcare, public sector or manufacturing. 
 Experience using platforms such as Salesforce and Jira. 
 Experience working within organizations where processes and tooling are actively evolving. 
 Why Vocantas? 
 Make a visible impact: join a small team where your decisions, ideas, and improvements can directly influence the customer experience. 
 Own the customer relationship: become the person your accounts rely on, from ongoing partnership and guidance to solving day-to-day issues.

 Entrepreneurial Energy: No two days look the same. You’ll work on meaningful problems with real business impact. 
 High Autonomy, High Impact: Own your work from Day 1 in a team that trusts you to deliver.

The idea of credit predates coinage itself. In ancient Babylon, loans of grain and silver were recorded on clay tablets, complete with interest rates, repayment terms, collateral, and the names of witnesses. These early systems turned trust into something durable and transferable, allowing people to invest in crops, businesses, and trade before they had the resources in hand. Nearly four thousand years later, credit still serves the same fundamental purpose: giving people and businesses the ability to act today based on what they can repay tomorrow. Now, people aren’t using silver—they are using Mercury.
 Modern credit cards make that promise feel instantaneous, but the systems behind them are anything but simple. Every transaction sits at the intersection of real-time authorization, credit risk, account servicing, repayment, interest, rewards, disputes, and regulation. Customers expect credit to work everywhere, immediately, while trusting that their account balance is accurate, their payments are applied correctly, and their business has access to capital when it matters most. 
 At Mercury, credit cards are an essential part of how ambitious companies manage spending and access capital. The Credit Card team builds and operates the credit-specific systems behind that experience—from credit account creation and lifecycle management to balances, statements, payments, interest, delinquency, and the controls that keep the product safe and compliant. As Mercury expands its credit offerings and pursues a bank charter, this team will help define what a modern, bank-grade credit platform should look like.

 Business Intelligence and AI-Enabled Self-Service 
 About the Role
 McKesson's Workforce Intelligence team transforms workforce data into clear, trusted insights that help leaders make better decisions. We combine high-quality business intelligence, thoughtful analysis, and practical technology enablement to make workforce information easier to access, understand, and use.
 As a Senior Workforce Intelligence Analyst, you will design and deliver visualization, reporting solutions, data products, and decision-ready insights across key workforce topics. You will translate business needs into intuitive analytical experiences, connect and model data, define meaningful metrics, and help stakeholders confidently interpret and act on workforce information.
  You will use approved AI capabilities to improve the speed, quality, and accessibility of BI work, and you will help build agentic and conversational solutions that enable responsible self-service for defined Workforce Intelligence use cases. When advanced data science is appropriate, you will partner with data science, technology, privacy, legal, and governance teams.
 Key Responsibilities
 Business Intelligence and Reporting
 ·         Design, develop, and maintain intuitive dashboards, reports, scorecards, and data products using Power BI or similar business intelligence platforms.
 ·         Translate business questions into clear analytical requirements, data models, measures, visualizations, and user experiences.
 ·         Build scalable, reusable reporting solutions that balance enterprise consistency with the needs of specific stakeholder groups.
 ·         Analyze workforce data to identify meaningful trends, patterns, relationships, and opportunities across topics such as workforce composition, talent movement, retention, recruiting, engagement, and organizational health.
 ·         Develop concise narratives and recommendations that connect analytical findings to business decisions and actions.
 ·         Continuously improve reporting solutions based on user feedback, adoption, changing priorities, and evolving business needs.
 Data Preparation, Modeling, and Quality
 ·         Combine and transform data from multiple HR and business sources into reliable datasets for analysis and reporting.
 ·         Develop and maintain semantic models, calculations, metric definitions, and reporting logic that support consistent interpretation of workforce information.
 ·         Write and optimize SQL queries and use appropriate data preparation tools to support reporting and analysis.
 ·         Validate data, investigate discrepancies, document business rules, and partner with data owners to resolve quality issues.
 ·         Apply data governance, privacy, security, and access requirements throughout the design and delivery of workforce intelligence products.
 ·         Maintain clear documentation for data sources, definitions, transformations, assumptions, and known limitations.
 AI-Enabled Productivity and Self-Service
 ·         Use approved AI assistants to support activities such as requirements synthesis, code development, documentation, quality checks, insight summarization, and content refinement, with appropriate human review.
 ·         Design and help build agentic, conversational, or natural-language solutions that enable users to access and navigate approved Workforce Intelligence content and use cases through self-service.
 ·         Ground AI-enabled experiences in governed data, approved metrics, curated knowledge, role-based access, and clear business rules.

The future of Lyft is a hybrid network, where autonomous vehicles and human drivers serve riders side by side on one platform. That future has already started. In September 2026, Lyft riders in Nashville were matched with Waymo autonomous vehicles on the Lyft app for the first time, a milestone years in the making. Through Flexdrive, Lyft manages the depots, charging and maintenance that keep autonomous fleets on the road. Our partnerships now span Waymo in Nashville, May Mobility in Atlanta and Baidu in Europe, with more on the way.
 We are early, and the playbook for running a hybrid marketplace at scale hasn't been written yet. You will help write it.
 The Global Growth organization is charting the future of Lyft's growth beyond North American rideshare's core products. This includes our premium Luxury modes and Livery drivers, building a unified Lyft presence internationally, and bringing Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) to riders domestically and abroad. As the Staff Data Scientist for AV, you will be the science leader for one of the most strategic bets at the company. You will set the vision for how we measure, optimize and grow autonomous rides on Lyft, and you will shape the strategy behind which partners we work with, which markets we enter and which products we build to win.
 This is a high-visibility role with direct exposure to Lyft's executive team and to our AV partners. You will work closely with engineering, product, operations, policy and partnership leaders, act as the bridge to our central marketplace science teams, and represent Lyft science in working sessions with partner teams. You will also have the opportunity to grow and define the AV science function as it scales.
 The ideal candidate is a thought leader who pairs deep technical rigor with strong business judgment. You are as comfortable designing an experiment or building a causal model as you are walking a senior leader through a recommendation. In this role, you will help us tackle problems such as:
 Hybrid matching: When a rider requests a ride, how should the marketplace decide between an AV and a human driver, and how does that choice affect wait times, AV utilization and driver earnings?
 Incrementality: What is the true incremental value of an AV ride to Lyft, beyond the ride itself, and how do we translate partner metrics into Lyft's topline?
 Rider trust and adoption: What makes a rider choose, trust or opt out of an autonomous ride, and how should the product experience earn that trust?
 Partnership performance: What shared metrics and service quality guardrails should define success with each AV partner, and how do we use them to improve the product together?
 Expansion strategy: Which markets, partners and use cases (such as airports) should we launch next, how large is each opportunity, and what does it take to win?
 Fleet economics: How do depot, charging and maintenance decisions shape AV availability, and where does Lyft's fleet operations model create the most value?
 The global picture: How does our autonomous roadmap fit with international expansion and our premium modes?
 Responsibilities: 
 Set the multi-year science vision and roadmap for AV at Lyft, and align engineering, product and partnership leaders around it
 Define the metrics framework for AV success, including incrementality, service quality and rider experience, and drive it into partner reviews and executive reporting
 Design and lead experiments and causal analyses on AV products, from rider onboarding to matching to post-ride experience
 Partner with central marketplace science teams to shape matching, pricing and supply models that work for a hybrid network
 Build the market sizing and business cases that guide where Lyft launches AVs next
 Represent Lyft science with AV partners and turn joint data into product improvements
 Mentor data scientists and analysts across Global Growth and help build the AV science team
 Experience: 
 Advanced quantitative background: Master's or PhD in Economics, Statistics, Operations Research, Applied Math, Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent high-impact industry experience
 7+ years in applied data science or applied science, with a track record of work that changed product direction or business strategy
 Deep, hands-on experience with causal inference and experimentation, including experiment design in two-sided marketplaces, counterfactual analysis and measuring incrementality
 Experience setting the technical direction for a product area and influencing roadmaps across multiple teams
 Experience presenting to senior executives and external partners, and turning complex analysis into clear decisions
 Strong proficiency in Python and SQL
 Nice to have: experience in autonomous vehicles, robotics, mobility, logistics or delivery; optimization or marketplace modeling; fleet operations or unit economics; international market expansion
 Skills 
 Ability to think strategically about complex, unstructured problems and turn them into a clear science roadmap
 Ability to choose the right method for the decision, and to explain the trade-off between rigor and speed
 Ability to break down large, messy datasets, including data shared by external partners, and synthesize inputs from multiple sources
 Ability to craft a compelling story and concisely present recommendations to technical and non-technical audiences, including senior leadership
 Ability to lead, influence and inspire others without formal authority in a fast-moving and ambiguous environment
 Strong product and user experience sense, with real curiosity about how riders experience a new technology
 Entrepreneurial self-starter who takes ownership, spots opportunities early and does what it takes to drive results
 Benefits:

Platform & Infrastructure keeps everything else fast, reliable and easy to build on. We own the shared services every product team builds on top of (identity, search, communication and our Pantry design system), the tooling that makes our engineers productive, and the release and runtime foundations that let us ship with confidence. Build it once, and every team benefits.

TEAMS YOU MIGHT JOIN

 - Product Foundation: Identity, communication, search and Pantry, including the Integrations Marketplace, Global Search and the Pantry Design System.

 - Developer Productivity: Internal tooling and IDE plugins that make every engineer faster.

 - Release + Runtime and Testing: CI/CD, SRE, FedRAMP compliance and QA. This team leans more toward infrastructure and reliability.

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

 - Build and evolve the shared services and components that other teams depend on.

 - Design APIs, tools and design system components that other engineers want to use, and support teams as they adopt them.

 - Improve the speed, safety and reliability of how we build, test and ship software.

 - Ship features end to end, from planning through production.

 - Partner directly with Product Managers, Designers, and the engineers who build on your work to shape your team's roadmap, not just execute against it.

 - Review code and mentor other developers on your team.

About 1Password

We’re looking for a Staff Product Manager to lead the enterprise readiness and platform modernization strategy for SaaS Manager, 1Password’s product for helping organizations discover, understand, and govern the applications their employees use. You’ll shape a multi-quarter roadmap across data ingestion, integrations, reliability, admin experiences, and responsible Artificial Intelligence (AI) capabilities, connecting deep technical decisions to customer and business outcomes. Reporting to the Director of Product, SaaS Manager, this remote role is open to candidates based in the United States or Canada.

How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.

What we're looking for:

• 8+ years of product management experience, including end-to-end strategy and roadmap ownership for Business-to-Business (B2B) Software as a Service (SaaS) products.

• Technical fluency with integrations, application programming interfaces (APIs), data pipelines, platform architecture, and the trade-offs involved in building for enterprise scale.

•  Strong product discovery, problem framing, iterative validation, prioritization, and success measurement skills.

• Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain recommendations, trade-offs, and risks to both technical and non-technical audiences.

• Experience with SaaS management, license management, IT asset management, identity and access management, cybersecurity, or other technically complex enterprise products.

• Experience with third-party SaaS ecosystems, including single sign-on (SSO), System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM), OAuth, audit logs, or similar integration patterns, as well as responsible AI-assisted product development.

What you can expect:

• Own the product strategy, roadmap, and prioritization for SaaS Manager’s platform modernization and enterprise readiness initiatives.

• Lead discovery with customers, internal partners, and data to identify the highest-impact enterprise problems and workflows.

• Determine how capabilities such as data ingestion, near-real-time processing, integrations, observability, and admin experiences should be sequenced to deliver customer value.

• Partner with Engineering and Design to evaluate architecture options, clarify requirements, and translate complex problems into shippable milestones.

• Define success metrics and work with Product Analytics and Data partners to measure reliability, adoption, customer impact, and business outcomes.

• Align multiple Product and Engineering teams around priorities, decisions, dependencies, and delivery risks.

• Coordinate launches, go-to-market readiness, customer feedback, and ongoing iteration as the product evolves.

JOB DESCRIPTION: 
 À propos d’Abbott 
 Abbott est un chef de file mondial de l’industrie des soins de santé qui crée des solutions scientifiques révolutionnaires visant à améliorer la santé des gens. L’entreprise est résolument tournée vers l’avenir, à l’affût des changements qui pourraient survenir dans le domaine des sciences et des technologies médicales.
 Être à l’emploi d’Abbott 
 En étant à l’emploi d’Abbott, vous pourrez faire un travail qui compte, vous perfectionner et apprendre, prendre soin de vous et des membres de votre famille, rester fidèle à ce que vous êtes et vivre pleinement. Vous pourrez :
 profiter de possibilités d’avancement professionnel au sein d’une entreprise internationale qui vous permettra de bâtir la carrière dont vous rêvez; 
 travailler pour une entreprise reconnue dans des douzaines de pays partout dans le monde comme étant un excellent milieu de travail et figurant parmi les entreprises les plus admirées dans le monde dans le classement Fortune; 
 travailler pour une grande entreprise reconnue comme étant l’une des meilleures où travailler, notamment pour ce qui a trait à la diversité du personnel, à la conciliation travail-famille ainsi qu’à la place des femmes dans les postes de cadres et les postes scientifiques. 
 L’occasion à saisir 
 Ce poste est au Québec et soutient le travail sur le terrain au sein de notre division cardiologie structurelle. La mission de notre activité en cardiologie structurelle est de restaurer la santé et d’améliorer la qualité de vie grâce à la conception et à la fourniture de dispositifs et de solutions de gestion destinés au traitement des maladies cardiaques structurelles.
 À titre de Spécialiste clinique, vous allez promouvoir et soutenir les produits Abbott de cardiologie structurelle, avec un accent particulier sur Navitor Vision™, par l’éducation des clients actuels et potentiels ainsi que par la couverture des procédures au Québec et est du Canada. Cela se fait par la prestation de formation clinique et de soutien aux ventes afin de contribuer à l’atteinte des objectifs de ventes projetés et à l’augmentation des revenus générés par les gammes de produits assignées. Un soutien additionnel à l’extérieur du territoire défini peut être requis selon les besoins de l’entreprise.
 La ou le Spécialiste clinique démontre une solide compétence clinique, assure une approche centrée sur le patient, maintien des normes élevées en matière de résultats cliniques et soutient activement le gestionnaire de comptes dans l’identification des opportunités et des enjeux au sein des comptes existants et potentiels, tout en contribuant à l’atteinte des objectifs d’affaires et à l’augmentation des revenus.
 Ce que vous ferez 
 Agir à titre de ressource principale pour le soutien clinique lors de procédures, incluant le soutien actif dans des environnements à haute pression, et orienter efficacement le comportement des médecins dans le cadre clinique 
 Collaborer avec le gestionnaire de comptes et le spécialiste du développement du marché afin d’élaborer et de mettre en œuvre la stratégie territoriale et les corridors de référence visant à accroître l’accès des patients et la croissance procédurale; démontrer une compréhension approfondie de l’activité des comptes ainsi que de leur performance actuelle et historique 
 Former les cardiologues interventionnels, le personnel des laboratoires de cathétérisme et le personnel de soutien sur les avantages et l’utilisation clinique appropriée des produits de cardiologie structurelle; offrir un soutien technique aux médecins durant les procédures et assurer la formation du personnel hospitalier et des médecins référents, entre autres 
 Communiquer les données produits, cliniques et de marché aux parties prenantes appropriées et soutenir les efforts de l’entreprise dans le développement et la mise en œuvre des stratégies de mise en marché; informer les clients des plus récentes avancées en matière de produits, de thérapies et de technologies, participer aux discussions cliniques, procédurales et techniques, et relier les résultats cliniques aux messages clés 
 Rencontrer les clients existants et potentiels afin d’identifier les besoins cliniques, les objectifs et les contraintes liés aux soins des patients, et proposer des solutions créatives et réalisables; établir et maintenir des relations au sein de divers départements hospitaliers (coordonnateur des valves, chirurgie, approvisionnement, vice‑présidence de la cardiologie, administration hospitalière, etc.) et identifier les décideurs clés afin de faciliter les ventes futures 
 Collaborer avec divers intervenants et médecins au sein du centre (cardiologues interventionnels, cardiologues en échocardiographie, anesthésiologistes cardiaques, chirurgiens cardiovasculaires, gestionnaires de laboratoires de cathétérisme, etc.) afin de générer des références, d’optimiser la planification des procédures et d’assurer de bons résultats cliniques pour les patients

 Respecter les exigences de conformité dans un environnement réglementaire en constante évolution (interne et externe) et répondre aux obligations de conformité internes et externes 
 Maintenir une valeur ajoutée pour le client en s’assurant que l’expertise est reconnue comme étant de haut niveau dans la thérapie et l’industrie; investir de façon proactive dans le développement professionnel afin de demeurer pertinent. 
 Déplacements requis jusqu’à 80 % du temps, selon la région, le territoire et la thérapie assignée. 
 Compétences requises 
 Diplôme d’études collégiales requis, baccalauréat préféré. 
 De 1 à 3 ans d’expérience pertinente. 
 Expérience privilégiée en milieu hospitalier ou dans un rôle similaire (de préférence en cardiologie interventionnelle – salle de cathétérisme cardiaque – ou dans un environnement technique au sein d’une entreprise du secteur des soins de santé). 
 Expérience des procédures cardiovasculaires en milieu hospitalier considérée comme un atout important. 
 Expérience en salle de cathétérisme cardiaque ou autre expérience technique hospitalière, un atout. 
 Excellentes aptitudes en présentation, en leadership et en coaching, ainsi qu’une capacité à évoluer dans un environnement complexe. 
 Expérience dans la mise en œuvre et l’exécution de programmes destinés aux professionnels de la santé et à d’autres parties prenantes.

 Connaissance des technologies endovasculaires, un atout majeur.

 Nous livrons des résultats – Vous assumez la responsabilité de votre travail, respectez vos engagements et vous concentrez sur la production de résultats concrets. Vous êtes responsable de vos actions et cherchez constamment à vous améliorer. 
 À quoi ressemble votre journée: 
 Superviser et coordonner toutes les activités du service pour assurer un traitement rapide et exact.
 Les tâches administratives du service comprennent l’ouverture et la tenue de comptes, le service à la clientèle, l’établissement des renseignements bancaires pour les TEF, les rapprochements liés au système, les lettres de bienvenue, la distribution du courrier, le classement et la numérisation.
 Gérer tous les dossiers de clients transmis à un niveau supérieur (interne/externe) et veiller au maintien du niveau de service à la clientèle au sein du service.
 Mettre en place des contrôles de qualité et faciliter la réalisation régulière de tests d’assurance qualité.
 Recueillir et analyser les principales mesures de rendement pour le service. Fournir des résumés de l’activité globale au cours du mois, en identifiant les circonstances uniques qui ont une incidence sur le service et les événements futurs prévus.
 Recommander des façons de simplifier ou d’améliorer les processus, s’il y a lieu.
 Maintenir une connaissance à jour de la réglementation du secteur.
 Mettre à jour les schémas de processus et les manuels de procédures conformément aux changements apportés à la réglementation, aux processus et au flux de travail.
 Surveiller la charge de travail du service et évaluer les besoins pour gérer les changements de volumes. Gérer les ressources en hiérarchisant les fonctions et en réaffectant les ressources afin de respecter les délais fixés.
 Offrir de la formation et un soutien continu aux membres du personnel nouveaux et existants.
 Fournir une rétroaction efficace et continue sur le rendement aux membres du personnel.
 Animer les réunions du personnel afin de faire le point sur les activités du service et d’encourager le partage d’idées, en sollicitant des sujets de conversation pertinents pour l’équipe.

 Études postsecondaires et formation continue dans le secteur des placements, en particulier les fonctions d’un service des opérations.

 Solides compétences en analyse et en résolution de problèmes et capacité à gérer plusieurs tâches avec le souci du détail approprié.

 Forte motivation et volonté d’obtenir des résultats.
 Compétences informatiques intermédiaires dans MS Word, Excel, Outlook, Access.
 Benefits 
 Pourquoi Aviso ? 
 Chez Aviso, vous trouverez une culture dynamique et inclusive qui valorise l’innovation et met en valeur les réussites de ses employés.
 Quelques traits qui nous distinguent : 
 Un programme de rémunération concurrentiel qui récompense et valorise les contributions de chacun.
 Des prestations de santé, soins dentaires et une assurance de premier plan pour satisfaire les divers besoins de nos employés

 Des cotisations complémentaires pour notre programme de retraite.

 Des événements sociaux organisés régulièrement pour favoriser le travail d’équipe.

 Politique d’égalité d’accès à l’emploi 
 Aviso accueille et encourage les candidatures de toutes les personnes qualifiées, y compris les candidats/titulaires handicapés. Si vous nécessitez un accommodement, nous travaillerons avec vous pour répondre à vos besoins à toutes les étapes du processus d’embauche.
 Nous remercions tous les candidats de leur intérêt, cependant, seules les candidatures retenues pour une étude plus approfondie seront contactées.
 Aucun recruteur ou agence, s’il vous plaît.
 Aperçu de la société 
 Fort d’un actif total sous administration et sous gestion environ 145 milliards de dollars, et d’un effectif de plus de 1 000 employés, Aviso est un important fournisseur de services de gestion de patrimoine et de placement pour le secteur financier canadien. Nous sommes fiers de propulser les entreprises qui renforcent le pouvoir des investisseurs.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Inference Router team at Cerebras builds the systems that decide where every inference request runs. We route traffic across all of Cerebras’ data centers and third-party integrations, balancing heterogeneous compute, maximizing cache utilization, and delivering the industry’s lowest time-to-first-token (TTFT) at massive scale.

As an Engineering Manager, Inference Router, you will lead the team responsible for the intelligent control plane of the fastest generative AI inference platform in the world. Your team owns global request routing, prefill/decode (P/D) disaggregation, prefix-aware routing for high cache hit rates, autoscaling, and the high-availability infrastructure that keeps the platform fast and reliable under real-time, bursty load.

This role operates at the intersection of distributed systems, Kubernetes-based infrastructure, routing-algorithm design, and machine learning. It combines technical leadership, people management, and execution ownership, with direct impact on the latency, throughput, and reliability experienced by every Cerebras inference customer.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

TECHNICAL LEADERSHIP

 - Own the architecture and evolution of the inference routing layer across all Cerebras data centers and third-party inference integrations.

 - Guide the design of:
   
   - global, multi-region request routing and load balancing;
   
   - routing for heterogeneous compute, including prefill/decode (P/D) disaggregated serving;
   
   - prefix-aware / cache-aware routing to maximize KV-cache reuse and utilization;
   
   - low-TTFT, high-throughput request scheduling under concurrent, bursty workloads.

 - Drive the routing algorithms that trade off cache locality, queueing, load, and latency in real time.

 - Invest in simulation: build high-fidelity models of the fleet and its workloads so the team can validate routing policies, failover behavior, and scaling decisions under a wide range of conditions without tying up precious accelerator capacity.

 - Partner with inference runtime, cloud/platform, hardware, and ML teams to optimize end-to-end performance.

TEAM LEADERSHIP

 - Build, manage, and grow a team of distributed systems, infrastructure, and ML systems engineers.

 - Provide technical direction, mentorship, and career development.

 - Foster a culture of ownership, velocity, and operational excellence.

 - Recruit top talent in distributed systems, Kubernetes/infrastructure, and routing/ML systems.

EXECUTION & DELIVERY

 - Drive execution of complex, cross-functional initiatives spanning inference runtime, cloud/infrastructure, and ML teams.

 - Own delivery of capabilities such as:
   
   - prefix- and cache-aware routing policies;
   
   - P/D-disaggregation-aware scheduling and placement;
   
   - autoscaling and capacity management across heterogeneous fleets;
   
   - high availability, failover, and graceful degradation;
   
   - simulation and load-generation frameworks that exercise the router under diverse traffic patterns, failure modes, and fleet topologies — without consuming scarce production compute;
   
   - observability, SLOs, and reliability across the routing stack.

 - Ensure high-quality releases through strong testing, load/chaos validation, and operational rigor.

PLATFORM & PERFORMANCE OWNERSHIP

 - Scale the routing layer to handle very large volumes of concurrent requests at the lowest possible latency.

 - Drive improvements in TTFT, throughput, cache-hit rate, and compute efficiency across the fleet.

 - Design for reliability and high availability: failover, redundancy, scale-out, and fail-closed behavior under partial outages.

 - Identify and prioritize technical debt and system bottlenecks.

 - Maintain Cerebras’ industry-leading inference speed advantage.

CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION

 - Partner with:
   
   - inference runtime teams (execution and serving);
   
   - cloud/platform and SRE teams (deployment, scaling, reliability);
   
   - ML researchers and engineers (model enablement, routing signals);
   
   - third-party integration partners.

 - Act as a bridge between infrastructure, routing, and production systems.

WHAT YOU BRING

 - 8+ years of experience in large-scale software engineering, distributed systems, or infrastructure.

 - 2+ years of engineering management experience.

 - Strong programming skills in C++ and/or Go for performance-critical, concurrent production systems.

 - Deep experience operating production services on Kubernetes: deployments, autoscaling, rollout strategies, and multi-cluster/multi-region topologies.

 - Proven track record building and operating highly available, scalable systems: load balancing, failover, scale-out, and reliability engineering.

 - Experience designing or operating request routing, load balancing, scheduling, or traffic-management systems at scale.

 - Experience with cloud infrastructure and best practices for building scalable microservices.

PREFERRED SKILLS

 - Experience with large-scale LLM/inference serving and the systems around it (e.g. vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, SGLang, or comparable).

 - Familiarity with prefill/decode (P/D) disaggregation, KV-cache management, and prefix/cache-aware routing.

 - ML background: understanding of inference workloads, batching, and the performance characteristics of serving LLMs and multimodal models.

 - Experience with autoscaling and capacity management across heterogeneous compute.

 - Experience building simulation, modeling, or load-testing frameworks for distributed systems to validate behavior cost-effectively at scale.

 - Strong grounding in observability (metrics, tracing, SLOs) and incident response for high-traffic production systems.

WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

The Inference Router is the control plane behind Cerebras’ core promise: the fastest AI inference in the world. The routing decisions your team makes — across data centers, across heterogeneous compute, with cache-awareness and high availability — directly determine the latency, throughput, and reliability every customer experiences. Your work keeps real-time AI applications fast and dependable, and unlocks new capabilities across enterprise and frontier AI use cases.

Why Join Cerebras

About Behavox 
 About the Role 
 The Senior FP&A Analyst owns Behavox's core financial model — its architecture, the accounting beneath it, and the forecasts and analysis the company plans and decides by. The role exists to change decisions, not report them: it turns the numbers into the choices leadership actually faces. It reads and integrates budgets into the model, but does not run the budgeting cycle.
 The same analyst builds the valuations, scenarios, and pro-forma models behind every acquisition — evaluating targets, running diligence, and folding closed deals into a single consolidated view. This work is periodic and must be carried alone when it arrives; the steady state is the operating model and SaaS forecasting.
 This is a high-autonomy role that works without a detailed brief and sets the modeling standard others build on. It is accountable for the accuracy and integrity of the numbers, and for turning them into recommendations sharp enough to act on — the downside case included, not just the point estimate — for senior leadership, the board, and investors. It pressure-tests the assumptions behind every result, works fluently with modern tooling and AI, and compounds that edge by learning relentlessly. Its influence comes from the rigor and reach of the analysis, not from authority: it owns the model and the truth it tells, not the decisions made from it.
 What You'll Bring 
 Financial Model & Accounting Foundations — Understands the architecture of integrated three-statement and operating models and the accounting that underpins them, including SaaS revenue recognition and cost treatment. Understands how the company's budgets are built and how to integrate them accurately into the core financial model.
 Forecasting & SaaS Unit Economics — Understands bottom-up short-term forecasting, driver-based long-term modeling, and the SaaS metrics that reveal business performance. Connects movements in those metrics to their underlying drivers and the operating levers that can change them.
 Mergers, Acquisitions & Integration — Understands acquisition valuation, purchase accounting, combined-entity projections, and consolidation mechanics sufficiently to evaluate targets and integrate completed acquisitions into the financial model.
 Business & Commercial Acumen — Understands in depth how the business and its functions generate revenue and incur costs, including the underlying revenue drivers, cost structure, and operating levers. Applies this knowledge to identify inconsistencies and challenge financial results and assumptions.
 Financial Systems & AI Tooling — Understands Google Sheets, Excel, AI, and automation capabilities sufficiently to determine how they should be applied to financial modeling and analysis. Distinguishes where automation can improve speed and control from where financial judgment and manual validation must remain.
 What You'll Do 
 Financial Model Ownership — Builds and maintains the core three-statement and operating model using robust architecture, accounting logic, scenario and sensitivity layers, and integrated budgets, owning the accuracy of every output and the integrity of every assumption to provide reliable forecasts and analysis for company planning and decision-making.
 Acquisition Modeling & Integration — Builds valuations, scenarios, and pro-forma combined-entity models by independently evaluating targets, supporting due diligence, and consolidating closed deals to provide a complete financial view of acquisition implications and the combined business.
 Business-Review Reporting — Drives the financial substance of monthly, quarterly, and annual business reviews with the broader FP&A team by translating model outputs and performance drivers into a clear narrative that enables senior management, the board, and investors to understand results and their implications.
 Metrics Analysis & Business Partnering — Diagnoses financial and SaaS metric movements by identifying operating drivers, pressure-testing assumptions, and modeling relevant levers and downside cases to give decision-makers evidence-based recommendations they can act on.
 AI-Enabled Productivity — Applies AI and spreadsheet automation to recurring financial workflows by automating appropriate work and strengthening data validation while retaining judgment over what remains manual to reduce cycle time without compromising financial integrity.
 What We Offer 
 A highly attractive benefits package, including competitive cash compensation, and an equity award aligned with long-term value creation.
 Modern, comfortable offices in Toronto and Montreal. This is a hybrid role (1 day in office). 
 About Our Process 
During the process we will begin by exploring the core factors regarding salary and location along with core experience and skills and values alignment. We will then deep dive explore the critical technical competencies we have identified for the role, and then we will deep dive in behavioral competencies.

About the Role

North Vector Dynamics is building next-generation defence systems, and we’re scaling fast: from prototype builds to production, from a handful of people to a full team, and through our next stages of growth and financing. We’re looking for a Director of Finance to build the finance function behind it: the planning, reporting, controls, and capital strategy that let us make good decisions quickly and prove to investors, customers, and auditors that we can be trusted with their money. Reporting to the CEO directly, you’ll own our budget, forecast, and cash runway, run month-end and year-end, and turn our books into the numbers leadership and the board steer by.

This is a ground-floor role for someone who is rigorous, commercially minded, and energized by building systems from a clean sheet rather than inheriting them. You’ll work side by side with every department head, our bookkeeping and accounting support, our investors and board, and senior leadership, and your work will shape how far and how fast this company can grow.

If you want to build the financial foundation for a company whose platforms will one day support operators in the field, save lives, and serve sovereign national interest - this role was written for you.

What You’ll Do

Financial Planning & Analysis

• Own the annual budget and rolling forecast: setting up cost centers, building department budgets with each head, and reporting budget-to-actual variances every month.

• Build and maintain the company financial model and cash runway, modelling hiring plans, capital spending (including our new manufacturing facility), and program scenarios so leadership can see the trade-offs before committing.

• Produce monthly management reporting for leadership and the board: P&L by cost center, burn, runway, program costs, and the KPIs that tell us whether we’re on track.

Accounting, Controls & Compliance

• Own month-end and year-end close, the general ledger, accounts payable and receivable, and payroll oversight, building on our current bookkeeping foundation and growing the accounting team as we scale.

• Design the internal controls a defence supplier is held to: approval authorities, purchasing and expense policies, segregation of duties, and an audit trail that holds up to scrutiny.

• Manage our annual financial statement audit or review, corporate income tax, GST, and claims under SR&ED and other government incentive programs.

• Lead program and contract finance: cost estimating and pricing support for bids, milestone billing, revenue recognition, and contract cost accounting that meets Government of Canada and allied customer requirements.

Capital, Investors & Systems

• Support fundraising and investor relations: board and investor reporting, data rooms, and financial due diligence for future rounds, and manage the cap table and equity plan administration with legal counsel.

• Find, secure and manage non-dilutive funding: government grants, contribution programs, and innovation funding that extend our runway.

• Run treasury and banking: cash management, foreign exchange for international suppliers, credit facilities, and corporate insurance.

• Lead the finance side of our ERP selection and rollout: chart of accounts, cost-center structure, and clean integration with purchasing, inventory, and manufacturing.

• Step into whatever the mission demands: this is a startup, and no two weeks will look the same.

What You Bring

Required

• A CPA designation (or similar) in good standing, with a degree in accounting, finance, or business.

• 10+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including at least 3 years leading a finance function or team, ideally in a manufacturing or hardware company.

• Hands-on FP&A experience: building budgets, forecasts, and three-statement financial models from scratch, and presenting them clearly to non-finance leaders.

• Deep experience with month-end close, financial reporting under ASPE or IFRS, external audits, and Canadian corporate tax.

• Experience supporting a venture-backed or high-growth company through financing rounds, board reporting, and investor due diligence.

• A track record of standing up accounting systems, internal controls, and policies that scaled with the business.

• Eligibility for a Government of Canada security clearance and registration under the Controlled Goods Program; active clearance is a significant asset.

• A builder’s mindset: you take ownership of the system, not just the task, and you’re as comfortable building a model at midnight before a board meeting as you are designing the process that makes it unnecessary next time.

Preferred

• Experience in a defence or aerospace company, including government contract costing, pricing, and audit (Public Services and Procurement Canada, DND, or US DoD contracts).

• Experience preparing SR&ED claims and managing IRAP, IDEaS, or similar non-dilutive funding programs.

• Manufacturing cost accounting experience: standard costing, inventory valuation, work in progress, and cost of goods sold.

• Experience with Series B or later financings, venture debt, or other growth capital.

• Experience with equity plan administration and cap table tools such as Carta.

• Multi-entity or international experience: US or European subsidiaries, foreign exchange, and transfer pricing.

Why North Vector Dynamics

• Real ownership from day one: the systems and processes you help build will be foundational to how this company operates for years to come.

• A tight-knit, high-calibre team that moves fast, holds each other to a high standard, and doesn’t waste time on bureaucracy for its own sake.

 Dans un contexte de croissance du portefeuille de projets et d'augmentation des besoins en analyse et en encadrement des demandes de projets, le bureau des projets TI de notre client souhaite renforcer sa capacité en analyse d'affaires afin de bien cadrer les besoins à la source des demandes de projets.
 La personne titulaire du poste collaborera avec plusieurs directions et intervenants afin de recueillir, documenter et valider les besoins d'affaires, évaluer la pertinence et la faisabilité des initiatives, soutenir la préparation des dossiers d'autorisation et assurer la qualité et la conformité des livrables. Le poste contribue au respect des exigences réglementaires et des processus de gouvernance du portefeuille, tout en favorisant l'optimisation des pratiques et la création de valeur pour l'organisation.
 Description du mandat 
 La personne titulaire du poste est responsable de soutenir la planification, la coordination et le suivi de projets visant l'amélioration et le développement des services. Elle assure un soutien professionnel aux différents partenaires en fournissant des conseils, un accompagnement méthodologique ainsi qu'un suivi rigoureux des activités qui lui sont confiées. Elle contribue activement à l'analyse d'affaires en technologies de l'information (TI), à la préparation des demandes de projets et au suivi de leur réalisation dans le réseau de la santé et des services sociaux, en veillant à ce que les projets présentés respectent les normes, les orientations stratégiques et les exigences réglementaires en vigueur.
 Principales responsabilités 
 Accompagnement à la rédaction de documents de projet (idée de projet, dossier d'opportunité, dossier d'affaires, et autres, au besoin) : 
 ●      Analyser les demandes de projet et évaluer leur conformité aux orientations stratégiques de l'organisation
 ●      Accompagner le demandeur pour bien formuler son besoin et réunir toutes les informations nécessaires dans les gabarits prescrits pour les étapes du processus d'autorisation du projet
 ●      Rédiger et réviser les documents de présentation de projets
 ●      Assurer le lien entre le demandeur et les équipes TI pour compléter les gabarits et informations techniques nécessaires à un dossier d'opportunité ou un dossier d'affaires concerté entre les parties prenantes
 ●      Soutenir les équipes de projets dans la production, l'optimisation et la conformité de la documentation légale et réglementaire exigée par les instances gouvernementales compétentes
 ●      Collaborer avec les différents intervenants pour collecter et valider l'information nécessaire à l'élaboration des projets
 ●      Assurer le suivi administratif des dossiers et soutenir les équipes dans les démarches liées au dépôt ou à l'acceptation des projets
 ●      Participer à l'application de la réglementation et à la mise en œuvre des standards et cibles définis par la direction
 ●      Agir comme catalyseur de simplification, en proposant des approches et des outils facilitants, orientés client
 ●      Contribuer à l'amélioration continue des processus liés à la gestion des demandes de projet
 ●      Planifier, préparer et animer les rencontres liées aux activités d'avant-projet et de planification de projet
 ●      Assurer un suivi des approbations et autorisations en identifiant des optimisations possibles
 Relations avec les clients et parties prenantes : 
 ●      Assurer un rôle-conseil auprès des demandeurs pour clarifier les besoins et bonifier la qualité des processus
 ●      Maintenir une communication continue et proactive avec les directions clientes
 ●      Promouvoir la transparence et la compréhension des processus d'intégration des projets au sein de l'organisation
 Exigences 
 ●      Diplôme universitaire de premier cycle dans un domaine pertinent (ex. : administration, analyse d'affaires, gestion de projet, santé publique, ou équivalent)
 ●      Expérience pertinente en analyse d'affaires dans le cadre de projets TI, de préférence dans le secteur de la santé ou des services sociaux
 ●      Connaissance des cadres réglementaires en gouvernance des ressources informationnelles et des enjeux liés au réseau de la santé et des services sociaux (atout)
 ●      Leadership mobilisateur et sens aigu de l'amélioration continue
 ●      Excellentes habiletés de communication
 ●      Excellentes habiletés rédactionnelles, d'analyse et d'organisation
 ●      Capacité à travailler en équipe multidisciplinaire et à gérer plusieurs dossiers simultanément
 ●      Capacité à gérer plusieurs projets ou mandats simultanément avec rigueur
 ●      Aptitude à naviguer dans l'ambiguïté et à prendre des décisions éclairées
 ●      Capacité à évaluer les besoins de la clientèle et à ajuster les services en fonction des contraintes organisationnelles
 Atouts 
 ●      Capacité à analyser les besoins numériques liés aux projets (ex. : systèmes de gestion des demandes, plateformes de gestion de projets ou outils spécialisés du réseau de la santé)
 ●      Aisance marquée avec les environnements numériques complexes et compréhension des principes de gestion et de sécurisation de l'information
 Conditions : 
 ●      Télétravail à 100 % (5 jours par semaine)
 ●      Horaire de jour, du lundi au vendredi (8 h 30 à 16 h 30)
 ●      Déplacements occasionnels possibles, sans frais supplémentaires pour la ressource

About AstraZeneca 
 At AstraZeneca, we are united by our purpose to push the boundaries of science to deliver life-changing medicines. We combine scientific excellence, deep disease area expertise, and a patient-focused mindset to transform the future of healthcare. As a leader within AstraZeneca Canada, the Vice President, Scientific Affairs will play a pivotal role in shaping the scientific and medical strategy for our Biopharmaceuticals portfolio and advancing our reputation as a trusted partner across the healthcare ecosystem. 
 Role Summary 
 The Vice President, Scientific Affairs is the senior Medical leader for AstraZeneca's Biopharmaceutical Business in Canada, accountable for defining and executing the country's Scientific and Medical strategy. This role oversees Medical Advisory, Field Medical, Regulatory Affairs, Evidence Generation, and Medical Excellence functions, ensuring the organization delivers best-in-class scientific leadership, regulatory excellence, and evidence generation across the portfolio. 
 As a key member of the Canadian Leadership Team, the VP will provide strategic guidance on emerging scientific trends, regulatory developments, and healthcare system dynamics while fostering strong relationships with external stakeholders, including Health Canada, key external experts, professional associations, academic centers, and healthcare institutions. 
 The role is responsible for developing high-performing teams, strengthening organizational capabilities, and partnering with regional and global colleagues to maximize patient impact and business performance. 
 Key Accountabilities 
 Scientific & Medical Leadership 
 Lead the Scientific and Medical strategy for the Canadian Biopharmaceutical portfolio. 
 Develop Medical plans that support lifecycle management and patient outcomes. 
 Serve as senior Medical advisor to the Canadian Leadership Team. 
 Provide scientific insight for business decisions and portfolio priorities. 
 Anticipate trends and align strategy with cross-functional partners. 
 Medical Affairs Excellence 
 Lead Medical Advisory, Field Medical, Evidence, and Excellence teams. 
 Drive scientific engagement, evidence generation, and communications. 
 Ensure medical activities are compliant, patient-centred, and aligned. 
 Advance medical capabilities and operational effectiveness. 
 Regulatory Affairs Leadership 
 Oversee Regulatory Affairs strategy and execution in Canada. 
 Guide submissions, approvals, and Health Canada interactions. 
 Respond to evolving regulatory and healthcare policy requirements. 
 Ensure regulatory compliance and portfolio risk management. 
 External Engagement & Scientific Influence 
 Build relationships with Health Canada and key external stakeholders. 
 Represent AstraZeneca in the scientific and healthcare community. 
 Communicate scientific evidence and support thought leadership. 
 Strengthen AstraZeneca's reputation as a trusted scientific partner. 
 Function Leadership 
 Lead and develop senior leaders and medical professionals. 
 Foster inclusion, innovation, accountability, and improvement. 
 Build succession plans and leadership pipelines. 
 Coach leaders to strengthen performance and talent development. 
 Manage budgets and resources to deliver priorities. 
 Maintain compliance with regulations, policies, and the IMC Code. 
 Ensure effective governance, risk, and compliance processes. 
 Essential Requirements 
 Degree in Medicine, Pharmacy, Life Sciences, or a related discipline. 
 Extensive pharmaceutical leadership experience in Medical or Regulatory. 
 Success leading complex Medical organizations and cross-functional teams. 
 Strong knowledge of the Canadian healthcare and regulatory landscape. 
 Strategic decision-making skills in highly matrixed organizations. 
 Experience building external scientific and healthcare relationships. 
 Strong budget management and resource allocation experience. 
 Deep knowledge of compliance requirements and the IMC Code. 
 Exceptional communication, influencing, and executive leadership skills. 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Licensed Physician (MD) strongly preferred. 
 MBA, MSc, PhD, or other advanced business or scientific qualification is an asset. 
 Experience engaging with global and regional Medical Affairs organizations. 
 Track record of leading through organizational transformation and capability building. 
 Why AstraZeneca 
 This is an opportunity to shape the future of healthcare in Canada by leading one of the country's most influential Scientific Affairs organizations. The Vice President, Scientific Affairs will have the opportunity to drive medical innovation, influence healthcare outcomes, develop exceptional talent, and help deliver life-changing medicines to patients across Canada.

ABOUT JUNIPER SQUARE

Private markets are one of the largest, most complex, and most underserved corners of global finance. Our mission at Juniper Square is to unlock their full potential. We’re the Operations Partner trusted by 2,300+ GPs, unifying technology, data, and fund administration services into a single platform that helps GPs move faster, make better decisions, and scale with precision. With $300B+ under administration and 700,000+ LPs on platform, we’ve built the scale to match our ambition. And with JunieAI, our purpose-built AI platform, we’re reimagining how private markets operate, embedding intelligence across every workflow. Founder-led since 2014, backed by $350M+ in funding, and now 1,000+ employees strong, we’re building a company designed to shape the future of private markets for decades to come.

ABOUT YOUR ROLE

Fund administration is one of the most important and fastest-growing areas of the Juniper Square business, and how we win there depends on product marketing expertise that sits shoulder-to-shoulder with Sales. We're seeking a Senior Product Marketing Manager, Fund Administration to partner with leadership on GTM strategy, as well as own the messaging, positioning, and enablement that move fund administration deals forward.

What sets this role apart: fund administration is a service, so understanding the offering means understanding the people who deliver it. You'll know our fund administration leaders and experts cold, including where each one is strongest, and you'll know our reference clients and how they differ across size, asset class, and profile. Keeping that picture current as the team scales fast is one of the most important parts of the job.

This role reports to the Head of Product Marketing and partners closely with Sales leadership and Pipeline.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

FUND ADMINISTRATION STRATEGY, POSITIONING & MESSAGING

 - Own Juniper Square's go-to-market strategy, positioning and messaging for the fund administration business unit, articulating a differentiated value proposition for each stakeholder in the buying group; CFOs, fund controllers, Heads of Finance and Fund Operations, leaders across investor services, accounting, treasury, compliance, and loan operations, and technical evaluators.

 - Position Juniper Square's fund administration service so buyers understand not just what it delivers but how it changes the way their teams work, and prepare Sales and Customer Success to have credible, informed conversations about it.

 - Build the fund administration persona and industry playbooks: buyer and influencer roles, priorities, objections, and content needs at every stage of the sales journey.

FUND ADMINISTRATION EXPERTISE & REFERENCES

 - Build and maintain a living map of Juniper Square's fund administration leaders and experts: who presents well, where each one is strongest, and who to bring into a given deal or moment.

 - Keep that picture current through constant data-gathering as the fund administration team grows fast, so sales always knows who to pull in and when.

 - Maintain deep knowledge of our fund administration reference clients and how they vary by customer size, asset class, and profile, so sellers can match the right proof to the right prospect.

FUND ADMINISTRATION LAUNCHES

 - Own every fund administration product and feature launch end to end with repeatable frameworks that scale from major product announcements to quarterly release moments.

 - Define what launch readiness looks like and drive the cross-functional plan that gets there, so each release lands with Sales, Customer Success, and the market ready.

 - Close the loop after launch, feeding adoption signal and customer feedback back to Product to shape what ships next.

SALES ENABLEMENT & DEAL SUPPORT

 - Work directly with Sales leadership and top sellers to co-create the collateral that wins fund administration deals: executive briefs, ROI narratives, competitive battlecards, demo narratives, and stakeholder-specific decks for each stage of the buying process.

 - Drive pipeline, upsell, and cross-sell velocity across the GP experience and fund administration suite, maintaining a cohesive release narrative that keeps prospects and customers engaged across the lifecycle.

 - Act as the internal expert on fund administration deal dynamics, playing an active role in shaping messaging and strategy on high-stakes opportunities.

VOICE OF CUSTOMER & COMPETITIVE INTELLIGENCE

 - Conduct deep voice-of-customer research through customer interviews, win/loss analysis, and Sales feedback to continuously enrich our understanding of fund administration personas and use cases across investor services, accounting, treasury, compliance, and loan operations.

 - Create the fund administration customer stories that validate our messaging with real-world proof.

 - Own competitive intelligence for the fund administration segment and disseminate actionable insights to Sales, Growth Marketing, and Product so the whole go-to-market motion stays aligned around how these teams actually buy.

BUILD AI-NATIVE

 - Use AI agents and tooling as core infrastructure to research accounts, synthesize customer and competitive inputs, which measurably accelerates the production of messaging and enablement assets.

 - Apply judgment to what AI produces: know where automation accelerates the work and where human insight matters.

QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3+ years of experience in or adjacent to fund administration is required (at a fund administrator, on a fund CFO, controller, or finance operations team, or at a company selling fund administration technology or services); you understand how these teams operate, who the buyers are, and what they care about.

 - Experience in B2B product marketing or GTM strategy roles is advantageous but not required, with a strong bias toward supporting Sales and influencing deal outcomes.

 - AI Fluency: experience using LLMs, agents, and AI automation tools to measurably accelerate your work, and understanding where human judgment is critical.

 - Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; the ability to translate nuanced market insights into clear, compelling GTM artifacts.

COMPENSATION

Compensation for this position includes a base salary, equity, and a variety of benefits. The U.S. base salary range for this role is $115,000 - $215,000 USD and the Canadian base salary range for this role is $85,000 - $137,000 CAD.
